title: The Early Malwa Forest Settlements Are Introduced

blocks.text: A fresh section opens under Episode About the Malwa and shifts from confederate campaigning to regional ancestry. The author places the story in Malwa's forests, tracing the setting through the descendants of Mehraj and Phool and the older territorial frame around fifty-two villages of Hisar Bawani.

This is a scene of frontier formation rather than settled sovereignty. The land is wooded, politically layered, and only partially domesticated, which is why lineage, patronage, and Guru-given legitimacy matter so much in the pages that follow.
The page functions as a regional prologue. Before individual heroes emerge, the reader is told what kind of place Malwa was and why its settlement had to be earned.
